panels.title: Pressure Stall (PSI)
panels.description: Watch: sustained plateaus, not spikes. OK: cpu/io < 5%, memory ≈ 0. Fix: grow infra(?)

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Watch: user/system/iowait and the steal line. OK: headroom below 100%, steal < 2–5%. Fix: user = Top Queries by CPU; system = use / configure properly a pooler; steal = hypervisor

panels.title: Load Average
panels.description: Watch: load1 vs the cores line. OK: load < cores. Fix: with low CPU% — processes queue on disk -> disk panels; with high CPU% -> CPU Usage

panels.title: Memory Available
panels.description: Watch: trend (MemAvailable = free + reclaimable cache; shared_buffers and hugepages excluded). OK: > 15–20%. Fix: pooler / lower work_mem * connections, add RAM; cross-check PSI memory — available can lie, PSI does not.

panels.title: Disk Latency
panels.description: Watch: per device, the WAL volume separately. OK: SSD/NVMe single-digit ms, > 10–20 ms is bad. Fix: growth at unchanged IOPS — disk

panels.title: Disk IOPS
panels.description: Watch: proximity to the volume limit, sawtooth in checkpoint rhythm. OK: < ~70% of the limit. Fix: find the consumer (pg_stat_io, tops), make longer checkpoints, raise volume class/size

panels.title: Disk Space Free
panels.description: Watch: worst volume trend — WAL/temp can eat space rapidly. OK: > 20–25%. Fix: WAL Directory Size (slot? archiver?) -> temp spills (Top Queries by Temp) -> bloat (pg_repack)

panels.title: Disk Queue Depth
panels.description: Watch: aqu-sz growth — it leads latency growth. OK: SATA/SAS SSD single digits, NVMe tens. Fix: as Disk Latency — find and spread the load, or a faster disk

panels.title: Swap I/O
panels.description: Watch: sustained swap-out (swap-in is just reading back). OK: 0. Fix: memory shortage — see Memory Available and PSI; vm.swappiness 1–10

panels.title: Swap / Dirty Memory
panels.description: Watch: dirty growth on a slow disk = incoming writeback storm; used swap never shrinks by itself. OK: dirty well below vm.dirty_bytes. Fix: lower vm.dirty_*_bytes, faster disk, spread checkpoints

panels.title: OOM Kills
panels.description: Watch: any value > 0. OK: strictly 0 — an OOM-killed backend = crash-recovery of the whole instance. Fix: victim in dmesg; vm.overcommit_memory=2

panels.title: Network Traffic
panels.description: Watch: NIC ceiling; spikes = replication/backups. OK: < ~70% of bandwidth. Fix: move backups/replication in time or to another interface; faster NIC

panels.title: Network Errors
panels.description: Watch: any sustained non-zero rate. OK: 0. Fix: driver/cable/MTU/ring buffers (ethtool) — infrastructure

panels.title: Hardware & Kernel Settings

targets.legendFormat: vm.overcommit_memory (rec. 2; with 0, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 is a must)
HugePages_Free (0 with PG running = pages taken by the DB)

panels.description: Watch: values diverging from the recommendation in the row name; a missing row means NOT collected (no include flag or the sysctl is absent in this kernel), not 'all good'. Fix: sysctl -w + /etc/sysctl.conf

options.content:
| what | recommended |
|---|---|
| THP | `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` → **never** (или madvise) |
| I/O scheduler | `/sys/block/<dev>/queue/scheduler` → **none** (NVMe) / **mq-deadline** (SSD) |
| readahead | `/sys/block/<dev>/queue/read_ahead_kb` → 128 OLTP / 2048–4096 аналитика |
| CPU governor | `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor` → **performance** |
| clocksource | `.../clocksource0/current_clocksource` → **tsc** |
| noatime | `mount \| grep <data-fs>` |
| Limit*/TasksMax | `/proc/<postmaster>/limits`, `systemctl show postgresql` |

Прод: снимать textfile-коллектором node_exporter (cron пишет `.prom`).

panels.title: PostgreSQL Up
panels.description: When the DB is down the pg_up series DISAPPEARS. Fix: exporter/network/database — collection health is up{job=~"sql-.*"}

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Watch: a sharp drop = restart/crash-recovery/failover (red — younger than 10 min). Fix: reason in PG logs; cross-check OOM Kills

panels.title: WAL Directory Size
panels.description: Watch: growth beyond max_wal_size. Fix: dead slot (Replication Slots), stuck archiver (WAL Archiver), checkpoints not keeping up

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Watch: client backends vs max_connections. OK: < 80%. Fix: pooler; who took the slots — Connections by Role.

panels.title: Checkpoints
panels.description: Watch: requested checkpoints appearing. OK: timed only. Fix: raise max_wal_size; who generates WAL — Top Queries by WAL.

panels.title: WAL Generation
panels.description: Watch: bytes/s, buffers_full, FPI share right after a checkpoint. Fix: buffers_full growing → raise wal_buffers; high FPI → wal_compression / less frequent checkpoints; culprit — Top Queries by WAL.

panels.title: Disk Writes by Backend
panels.description: Watch: who dominates — checkpointer/bgwriter/autovacuum/client. Fix: per culprit: spread checkpoints, vacuum cost, queries (Workload).

panels.title: Disk Reads by Backend
panels.description: Watch: client reads growing = the working set no longer fits in memory. Fix: RAM/shared_buffers; who reads — Top Queries by Buffer Misses / Disk Reads.

panels.title: WAL Latency
panels.description: Watch: ms/op — the main commit latency driver under sync replication. OK: fsync single-digit ms. Fix: the disk under WAL (Disk Latency, OS), separate volume, synchronous_commit.

panels.title: Buffer Evictions & Bgwriter
panels.description: Watch: evictions = pressure on shared_buffers; maxwritten_clean = bgwriter hitting its limit. Fix: raise shared_buffers, raise bgwriter_lru_maxpages.

panels.title: I/O Time by Backend
panels.description: Watch: seconds of IO per second per subsystem (can exceed 1 — parallelism). Fix: by the dominating subsystem — checkpoints/vacuum/queries.

panels.title: I/O Latency (pg_stat_io)
panels.description: Watch: ms/op vs Disk Latency (OS): matches — disk-bound; much lower — the page cache is saving you. Fix: as Disk Latency.

panels.title: Connections by Role
panels.description: Watch: which database/role ate the max_connections slots. Fix: pooler for the culprit, per-role connection limit.

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Watch: a sustained DOWNWARD trend, not the level. OK: > 99% for OLTP. Fix: RAM/shared_buffers; percentages deceive — cross-check absolute Disk Reads by Backend.

panels.title: Checkpoint & Block I/O Time
panels.description: Watch: checkpoint write/sync busy share and per-DB block IO time (can exceed 1). Fix: spread checkpoints; detailed attribution — I/O Time by Backend.

panels.title: Sessions by State
panels.description: Watch: idle growth — an app without a pooler; idle in transaction growth — a source of locks and bloat. OK: idle in tx ≈ 0. Fix: pooler; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.

panels.title: Locks
panels.description: Watch: the waiting series (granted=false) — the lock queue. OK: steadily 0 waiting. Fix: who holds whom — Blocking Sessions (Workload).

panels.title: Transactions
panels.description: Watch: a commit dip while waits grow = queued; rollback growth = errors/deadlocks/retries. Fix: DB Load (AAS) → by wait class.

panels.title: Deadlocks & Temp Files
panels.description: Watch: deadlocks/min > 0; temp bytes/s. Fix: deadlock — lock acquisition order in the app; temp — work_mem / the plan (Top Queries by Temp).

panels.title: WAL Archiver
panels.description: Watch: the .ready queue and last-success age — failed==0 with a STUCK archiver is false calm. OK: queue ≈ 0. Fix: archive_command/storage; a growing queue will fill the disk.

panels.title: SLRU Caches
panels.description: Watch: read/written spikes on SubtransSLRU/MultiXact — sudden degradation, visible in AAS only as an anonymous LWLock. Fix: long transactions with savepoints, SELECT FOR SHARE; PG17 — SLRU size GUCs.

panels.title: Long Transactions & 2PC
panels.description: Watch: transactions holding vacuum and xmin; forgotten prepared xacts. OK: prepared ≈ 0. Fix: kill/fix the client; COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED; apply pending restarts in a window.

panels.title: Session Errors & Checksums
panels.description: Watch: fatal/killed spikes; checksum > 0 = page corruption. OK: checksum strictly 0. Fix: checksum — disk/memory, restore from backup/replica; killed — find who kills (OOM? admin?).

panels.title: Instance Settings

targets.rawSql:
SELECT name,
       current_setting(name) AS value,
       CASE WHEN pending_restart THEN 'ЖДЁТ РЕСТАРТА' ELSE '' END AS pending,
       CASE WHEN source = 'configuration file' AND sourcefile LIKE '%postgresql.auto.conf'
            THEN 'ALTER SYSTEM' ELSE source END AS source
FROM pg_settings
WHERE name = ANY(ARRAY['max_connections','max_files_per_process','shared_buffers','effective_cache_size','work_mem','maintenance_work_mem','huge_pages','huge_page_size','shared_memory_size_in_huge_pages','max_wal_size','min_wal_size','checkpoint_timeout','checkpoint_completion_target','wal_buffers','wal_compression','synchronous_commit','synchronous_standby_names','autovacuum_max_workers','autovacuum_naptime','autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit','bgwriter_lru_maxpages','track_io_timing','track_wal_io_timing','shared_preload_libraries'])
ORDER BY array_position(ARRAY['max_connections','max_files_per_process','shared_buffers','effective_cache_size','work_mem','maintenance_work_mem','huge_pages','huge_page_size','shared_memory_size_in_huge_pages','max_wal_size','min_wal_size','checkpoint_timeout','checkpoint_completion_target','wal_buffers','wal_compression','synchronous_commit','synchronous_standby_names','autovacuum_max_workers','autovacuum_naptime','autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit','bgwriter_lru_maxpages','track_io_timing','track_wal_io_timing','shared_preload_libraries'], name)

panels.description: Watch: the pending-restart flag; source = ALTER SYSTEM vs configuration file; on standby — ITS OWN values. Live SQL, the datasource follows the instance selector (uid pg-${db}; on «datasource not found» revert to $pgds). Fix: restart in a window; cross-check hugepages with Hardware & Kernel Settings (OS).

panels.title: Transaction ID Age
panels.description: Watch: growth without a plateau = autovacuum can't freeze fast enough; the only metric able to stop the database entirely. OK: well below 200M. Fix: Xmin Horizon (who holds it), workers/cost limit.

panels.title: Tables Needing Vacuum
panels.description: OK: 0 to a few. Fix: workers/naptime/cost; growing while vacuum runs — xmin is held (Workload).

panels.title: Unused Indexes
panels.description: Watch: dead weight — a price paid on every UPDATE. Fix: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY after checking usage on replicas.

panels.title: Invalid Indexes
panels.description: OK: 0 (leftovers of a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY). Fix: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY or DROP+CREATE.

panels.title: Sequence Exhaustion
panels.description: OK: < 60%. Fix: migrate to bigint / setval; the label shows which sequence.

panels.title: Database Size
panels.description: Watch: trend breaks. Fix: the 'running out of space' route: WAL → temp → bloat.

panels.title: Table Size (top 20)
panels.description: Watch: a sharp break = bloat after mass UPDATE/DELETE. Fix: pg_repack.

panels.title: Dead Tuples
panels.description: Watch: growth while autovacuum runs = something holds it back. Fix: Xmin Horizon, workers.

panels.title: Seq vs Index Scans
panels.description: Watch: seq scans on large tables — index candidates. Fix: add an index; cross-check Top Queries by Buffer Misses.

panels.title: HOT Update Ratio

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (schemaname, relname) (rate(pg_table_activity_total{job=~"$db",op="tup_hot_upd"}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (schemaname, relname) (rate(pg_table_activity_total{job=~"$db",op="tup_upd"}[5m])), 0.001)

panels.description: Watch: < 100% on UPDATE-heavy tables = updates touch indexes. Fix: fillfactor < 100, don't index updated columns.

panels.title: Last Vacuum / Analyze
panels.description: Watch: -1 = never; a stale ANALYZE = stale planner stats = bad plans. Fix: ANALYZE, per-table autovacuum settings; cross-check Plan Flip Detector.

panels.title: Vacuum Progress
panels.description: Watch: a phase stuck for hours = a huge table or a throttled cost limit. Fix: raise vacuum_cost_limit / lower cost_delay; partitioning.

panels.title: Table Bloat
panels.description: Hourly estimate; dead tuples != bloat — vacuum frees no space back. Fix: pg_repack/VACUUM FULL; verify with pgstattuple before acting.

panels.title: Index Bloat
panels.description: Hourly estimate; vacuum does not shrink indexes. Fix: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY.

panels.title: Queries per Second
panels.description: Watch: a break vs baseline. Fix: growth with latency → tops; concentration — Top Queries by Calls.

panels.title: Query Latency (avg)
panels.description: Watch: the trend; the average hides tails — see Latency Spread. Fix: DB Load (AAS) → class → tops.

panels.title: Oldest Transaction / Query
panels.description: Watch: the oldest transaction holds vacuum; idle-in-tx holds locks. OK: seconds. Fix: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, statement_timeout, fix the client.

panels.title: DB Load (AAS)
panels.description: Watch: total height vs cores and the dominating class; a Lock-class plateau of height N = N sessions queued. OK: AAS < cores. Fix: Lock → Blocking Sessions; IO → Disk Reads/Writes by Backend + tops; CPU → Top Queries by CPU.

panels.title: Blocking Sessions

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  w.pid                                                   AS waiter_pid,
  bp.pid                                                  AS blocker_pid,
  w.usename                                               AS waiter_user,
  b.usename                                               AS blocker_user,
  b.state                                                 AS blocker_state,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - w.state_change)))::int AS wait_s,
  COALESCE(w.query_id::text, '')                          AS waiter_queryid,
  LEFT(regexp_replace(w.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 70)      AS waiter_query,
  LEFT(regexp_replace(b.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 70)      AS blocker_last_query
FROM pg_stat_activity w
CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(pg_blocking_pids(w.pid)) AS bp(pid)
JOIN pg_stat_activity b ON b.pid = bp.pid
WHERE w.wait_event_type = 'Lock'
ORDER BY wait_s DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.description: Empty = no lock queue. blocker_state = idle in transaction — the classic root cause. Live SQL as role monitoring (timeouts 5s/1s); the datasource follows the instance selector (uid pg-${db}; on «datasource not found» revert to $pgds). Fix: terminate the blocker, fix the client.

panels.title: Top Queries by Wait Time
panels.description: Ranks by total active time (CPU + waits), sees queries in flight. Fix: queryid → Query Text Lookup below.

panels.title: Top Wait Events
panels.description: Watch: the specific event — DataFileRead vs WALSync vs Lock:transactionid are different diseases of one class. Fix: per event.

panels.title: Top Queries by Time
panels.description: Share of DB time (can exceed 1 — parallelism). Fix: the culprit's plan — auto_explain (grep qid=).

panels.title: Top Queries by Calls
panels.description: Watch: traffic concentration in a handful of queries. Fix: client-side caching/batching.

panels.title: Latency Spread (p50–p99)
panels.description: Percentiles of per-query AVERAGES (not executions — pgss doesn't keep those). Watch: the p99/p50 gap = a few heavy queries against a fast mass. Fix: Top Queries by Time.

panels.title: Autovacuum Workers
panels.description: Watch: a plateau at the ceiling = saturation. Fix: raise autovacuum_max_workers/cost_limit.

panels.title: Xmin Horizon
panels.description: Watch: growth = vacuum is held back, dead rows pile up. Fix: find the holder — Long Transactions, slots, prepared.

panels.title: Top Queries by Rows
panels.description: Watch: rows/s as a proxy for over-fetch and network traffic; weight = rows per call. Fix: LIMIT/pagination, drop unneeded columns/rows client-side.

panels.title: Top Queries by Buffer Misses
panels.description: Reads past shared_buffers — possibly OS cache, NOT necessarily disk (physics — Top Queries by Disk Reads). Fix: indexes/RAM.

panels.title: Top Queries by Temp
panels.description: Who spills to disk. Fix: work_mem (careful: × connections), fix the plan (sorts/hashes).

panels.title: Top Queries by WAL
panels.description: Who generates WAL — the culprit of checkpoint storms and replication lag. Fix: batch UPDATEs, drop redundant indexes (each one = WAL).

panels.title: Top Queries by CPU

targets.legendFormat: вся БД (сверить с CPU хоста, слой 1)

panels.description: Real CPU (pg_stat_kcache); the whole-DB line — compare with host CPU Usage: whose CPU is it. Fix: the culprit's plan/JIT/functions.

panels.title: Top Queries by Disk Reads
panels.description: True physical disk (getrusage), OS cache not counted — unlike Top Queries by Buffer Misses. Fix: indexes, RAM, a faster volume.

panels.title: Plan Flip Detector
panels.description: Watch: stddev/mean growth at an unchanged rate = bimodal latency = the plan likely flipped. Fix: the plan in the auto_explain log (qid=), ANALYZE tables, pin the plan.

panels.title: Query Text Lookup
panels.description: Texts for top-10 by time/WAL/temp. For queryids from other tops — SQL straight into pgss (SELECT query FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE queryid = ...).

panels.title: Replication Lag (seconds)
panels.description: Watch: which stage lags. OK: for sync — milliseconds. Fix: write/flush — standby disk; replay — conflicts / single-threaded replay.

panels.title: Replication Lag (bytes)
panels.description: Watch: sent lag = network/walsender can't ship. Fix: network, standby disk.

panels.title: Sync Standbys
panels.description: OK: equals the count in synchronous_standby_names. Fix: 0 = COMMITS ARE STUCK — restore standby/network now or drop sync temporarily.

panels.title: WAL Receiver
panels.description: OK: 1. Fix: 0 = the stream is broken (network/slot/timeline) — replay lag may falsely read zero meanwhile.

panels.title: Replication Slots
panels.description: Watch: retained WAL growing = the slot consumer is dead; safe_wal_size shrinking = headroom to slot loss. Fix: revive the consumer or DROP the slot before primary's disk fills.

panels.title: Standby Replay
panels.description: Watch: gap bytes (received, not replayed) growing = replay is the bottleneck (single process/conflicts/disk); delay seconds while primary is idle is normal. Fix: conflicts (Recovery Conflicts), standby disk.

panels.title: Recovery Conflicts
panels.description: Watch: mostly snapshot/lock — standby queries cancelled by replay. Fix: hot_standby_feedback (price — bloat on primary) or max_standby_streaming_delay.

panels.title: Scrape Targets
panels.description: OK: all = 1. Fix: whichever job is down — that monitoring layer is blind; absent() alerts must catch this.

panels.title: Scrape Duration
panels.description: OK: well below the 10s timeout. Fix: close to 10s — a heavy collector; see rollback triggers in rollback_cumulative_stats.txt.

panels.title: Scrape Samples vs Limit
panels.description: Watch: approaching sample_limit — exceeding it drops the WHOLE scrape. Fix: cardinality (top-N, labels) or raise the limit in prometheus.yml (the 8000 line is hardcoded).

panels.title: pgss Evictions
panels.description: Watch: dealloc growth = top-N silently undercounts. Fix: raise pg_stat_statements.max or reset more often.

panels.title: TSDB Head Series
panels.description: Watch: growth steps = cardinality explosion. Fix: find the culprit via count by (__name__), sample_limit guards.
